reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Poisson.poissonMeasureENN
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: the law of N(A) for the Poisson random measure: Poisson with mean
lambda(A) = (dt x nu)(A) in [0, infinity]. A definition named poissonMeasureENN is presumably the
Poisson distribution as a probability measure on [0, infinity] (ENNReal), parameterized by a
mean lambda (in ENNReal or NNReal). Faithful: for finite lambda, the law
sum_{k >= 0} e^{-lambda} lambda^k / k! delta_k (the image of Mathlib's Poisson pmf under
N -> ENNReal), with lambda = 0 giving delta_0; for lambda = infinity (if the parameter admits it)
the Dirac mass delta_infinity, the standard convention for infinite-intensity sets. A junk value
for lambda = infinity, e.g. delta_0 or Poisson(0) through toNNReal infinity = 0, would be
unfaithful and dangerous: it would force N(A) = 0 a.s. for every infinite-intensity A, which is
impossible for a PRM with nu(E) = infinity (N((0,1] x E) >= N((0,1] x B_k) for finite-mass
B_k whose intensities tend to infinity), making every PRM with infinite-activity nu nonexistent
and all propositions over such PRMs vacuous - unless the PRM definition only applies this law to
finite-intensity sets. Must be a probability measure.

comparison.text:
Lean: poissonMeasureENN (mu : NNReal) : Measure ENNReal := (ProbabilityTheory.poissonMeasure
mu).map (fun n : N => (n : ENNReal)).
Comparison with the locked reading: for finite lambda = mu, the image of the Poisson(mu) law on N
under N -> ENNReal, i.e. sum_k e^{-mu} mu^k/k! delta_k; mu = 0 gives delta_0; a probability
measure (map of a probability measure along a measurable map from the discrete N). The parameter
type NNReal excludes infinity, so no junk case exists inside this definition; the infinite
intensity case is handled in PoissonRandomMeasure by the separate field
infinite_at_infinite_intensity (N(B) = top a.s.), and poisson_law applies poissonMeasureENN only to
finite intensities (toNNReal of a finite ENNReal is exact). The danger flagged in the reading
(delta_0 at infinite intensity) does not arise. Faithful.
